backend/tests/canary/conftest.py -- Patch Q06: the hermetic environment of the canary tests.

The canary session runs the REAL device client, which writes its store, its checkpoints and its logs under
``$M2C_HOME`` and reads ``$HOME``.  Both are pointed at a per-test temporary directory (the same thing m2c/tests/
conftest.py does for the client's own tests), so no test can read or create anything in the real ``~/.m2c``.

The backend's own tests/conftest.py (parent directory) still applies: it swaps ``memory.bus.redis`` for an in-memory
twin for every test, which the canary scan also looks at.

backend/tests/canary/harness.py -- Patch Q06: one scripted session of the REAL server and the REAL device, in process,
with a recorder at every place content could come to rest.

WHAT IS REAL AND WHAT IS FAKE
-----------------------------
Real, on the server: the device socket (codeagent/ws.py) served by uvicorn on 127.0.0.1, the message router, the run
handlers, the emitter, the tool broker, the agent loop (codeagent/loop.py) wired in by codeagent/wiring.py as
api/server.py wires it, the budgeted context assembler, metering, the run manager, the run store (see MODES) and the
encrypted run buffer (codeagent/buffer.py: real AES-GCM, real key derivation).

Real, on the device: the genuine C04 DeviceLink over a genuine TCP WebSocket, the tool runner, the policy engine, the
file and shell tools (real `bash` on a temporary project), checkpoints, the instruction loader (M2C.md goes into
run.start), the local SQLite store, and the terminal chat's session controller (m2c/tui/session.py) with a fake screen.

Fake: the model (loop_testkit.ScriptedAdapter: it streams text and proposes tool calls from a script), Redis (the repo's
in-memory twins, each wrapped so that every command is recorded), the person (an auto-approver of the approval prompts)
and, in fake mode only, Postgres (see MODES).

MODES (the two the repo's other database tests use; MINIME_TEST_DATABASE_URL decides)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  fake  No database URL.

backend/tests/canary/scanners.py -- Patch Q06: the scanners behind the "no content at rest" canary test.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
--------------------
The trust statement of the product (build plan section O1, 11.3, 11.4) is that the server keeps no prompt, no file
content, no path, no command and no tool output once a run is over, and never writes any of them to Postgres, to a
log, to an error report or to a metric.  A test of that statement is only worth something if a green result cannot be
produced by a scanner that looks in the wrong place or for the wrong shape.  So this module has two halves, and the
tests in this package use both:

  * the NEEDLES: for every planted canary, every form it commonly takes when it passes through a serializer (raw, the
    random token alone, JSON-escaped, JSON-in-JSON, URL-encoded, base64 and base64url at all three byte alignments,
    hex, Python escapes, UTF-16), the two halves of the random token (what is left when a canary is cut in two by a line
    break or a log prefix) and a "squashed" form that survives being wrapped;
  * the SCANNERS: one per place content could come to rest (Postgres rows, every SQL statement and parameter that a
    recording fake saw, application logs, Redis keys and values, error-reporting payloads, the usage ledger, and the
    device's own store, which is ALLOWED to hold content).  Each takes the thing to look at and returns hits; nothing in
    here asserts by itself, `assert_clean` does.

backend/tests/canary/test_no_content_at_rest.py -- Patch Q06: the "no content at rest" canary test.

This is the test that backs the product's trust statement (build plan O1): the server keeps no prompt, no file content,
no path, no command and no tool output once a run is over, writes none of them to Postgres, to a log, to an error
report or to a metric, and while a run is open keeps its content only in the encrypted run buffer.

HOW IT WORKS (details in harness.py and README.md next to it)
-------------------------------------------------------------
Every scenario plants fresh random canaries in the prompt, in the project's files, in tool output, in the model's reply,
in tool arguments (a path and a command), and in an instruction file (M2C.md, loaded into run.start).  It then runs one
scripted session end to end in this process: the real server code over a real WebSocket, the real device code in a
temporary project, a recorder at every storage place, the real logging configuration, and the error-reporting SDK
initialised with a transport that keeps what it would send.  Then every place content could rest is scanned for every
canary in every common encoded form (scanners.py).  A hit anywhere fails the test.

The scenarios: a normal finish (and `completed`), a cancel in the middle of a model answer, a disconnect during a tool
call and the resume, a failure of the model, a tool error, a quota pause, and a ledger failure (metering fails open).

backend/tests/canary/test_scanner_selftest.py -- Patch Q06: proof that a green canary result cannot come from a scanner
that looks in the wrong place.

test_no_content_at_rest.py scans nine kinds of place.  Here a canary is planted, on purpose, in EACH of them:

  * through the real recorders of the harness wherever one exists (a log record on the server's loggers, a Redis
    command on the run buffer's twin and on run_guard's, a SQL statement or store call, an error report captured by
    the real SDK, a row in a real Postgres table when a database URL is set, a row in the device's SQLite store), and
  * through the Result record that the checks read, field by field (so a field that stopped being checked is caught).

and the matching check must fail, naming the place.  It is then repeated for every encoded form that commonly slips
through (JSON-escaped, JSON in JSON, URL-encoded, base64 and base64url at all three alignments, hex, Python escapes) and
for a canary split across two log lines or two Redis values.  Finally a CLEAN run must pass the same checks, so the
checks are not simply always failing.

Everything is made at run time (gitleaks): canaries are random strings, never literals.
